summary: Nastes (Ancient Greek: Νάστης) son of Nomion is co-captain, with his brother Amphimachus, of the Carian contingent at Troy. Homer's Catalogue describes one of the brothers arriving all decked with gold; commentators disagree whether Achilles then slays Nastes or Amphimachus and strips the ornaments. He is lord of the Carians of Miletus in the atlas domains.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Amphimachus of Caria" · CC BY-SA 4.0

sections.heading: Carian co-captain
paragraphs: Iliad 2 names Nastes and Amphimachus, glorious children of Nomion, leaders of the Carians who held Miletus, leafy Phthires, Maeander's streams, and Mycale's crests. One brother comes to war decked with gold like a girl; the gold does not ward off destruction when Achilles kills him in the river.

Thomas Seymour's commentary takes Nastes as the gold-wearing victim; other readers leave the Catalogue's "he" ambiguous between the twins. The atlas keeps Nastes as Nomion's named co-captain without forcing that identification.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (nastes-nomionid) is Nomion's Carian son alone. His brother is amphimachus-nomionid; their father is nomion-carion. Wikipedia has no separate Nastes article — the house is covered under Amphimachus of Caria.
